items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I went with the Artie Shaw band in 1940. And now from ‘40 through ‘45 I think I played with three different Artie Shaw bands, and wrote arrangements and played trombone

ctx.x: I think you said a very important thing when you talked about how the ump-chick of your father playing instilled that rhythm in you. Because you can hear that in your arrangements. Do you think that’s one of the keys to what’s made your arranging so successful? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Well you know, you ask very good questions by the way. Up to that point that you’re talking about, when you started hearing my music, I wasn’t before that, prior to that, like when I went through the quote big band era, where I played with the bands like the first big band I played with was Bunny Berigan in 1938. I played trombone and arranged music as well for the band. Then I did the same thing with the Bob Crosby band in 1939, and then I went with the Artie Shaw band in 1940. And now from ‘40 through ‘45 I…

And bop was kind of supposed to be a floating type of rhythm on top cymbals and stuff. You weren’t supposed to hear it, you were supposed to feel it here. You were supposed to feel what he was trying — and I don’t know, I never felt that, so I said, “Hey you know, Harry, I just don’t feel that kind of music,” and you know, “maybe it’s time you got another boy.” And his jaw dropped. He looked at me and he couldn’t believe what I was saying. And he said, “well, okay.” So I left the band. For two years I thought all…

items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had three or four stars. I had Georgie Auld. I got Les Robinson back. Who was on drums? Nick Fatool on drums. Johnny Guarnieri on piano. It was a good band. The soloists were marvelous. There was Ray . . . Ray Conniff was very good on gutbucket trombone.

ctx.x: Which film was this? Second Ending?

Second Chorus. And Billy played Fred Astaire. Bobby for one reason or other didn’t want to go out with a band. Billy did. I paid him a lot. And then I wanted good bands, so I got Jack Jenney, who was on the loose. I got Lennie Hayton, who was . . . I used to work for him, in the Ipana program. The rest of the band were all good solid players. It’s like a football team. You get three or four stars and build the team around them. I had three or four stars. I had Georgie Auld. I got Les Robinson back. Who was on…
Did you . . . did the same feelings come back, that you had in ’39?
